investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota reached), and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 134–147 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner never received a running agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent, causing a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

[Likely secondary] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those nodes are saturated. The 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.
[Possible] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource in the target namespace is exhausted, preventing new allocations even if node-level capacity exists.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A recent change to the cluster node pool (e.g., node scale-down, node failure, or VM slot reconfiguration) reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.
[Low probability] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm was increased beyond what the nodes can satisfy per-pod, making scheduling impossible even on an otherwise idle cluster.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the capacity exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior probe's pod was released) and not a persistent saturation.

If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, the root cause is not capacity exhaustion but rather a misconfigured node affinity/selector or a quota boundary above the node level.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, the failure would be a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion — this would be visible in the pod spec and cluster event log.
If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message and the others had passed, a shared capacity exhaustion explanation would be weakened in favor of a transient scheduling race.
If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show zero allocated VM slots, the issue is that the pod's resource request quantity exceeds per-node capacity, not that slots are consumed by other pods.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation — this would surface capacity exhaustion as a distinct, earlier signal rather than a timeout.

Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote agent pods from prior eval runs remain in a non-terminal state after the withCleanup wrapper completes, catching pod leaks before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity-match eval that verifies at least one node satisfies the remote agent pod's affinity/selector requirements and carries non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, providing a fast structural health check independent of agent creation.

Consider adding a latency-band eval that fires a warning when remote agent pod scheduling exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) before the full 134s+ timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure before it becomes a hard failure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating zero available nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a pod, no agent was ever created, and the expected-output contract evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state were never populated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so the scheduler cannot place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Preemption is also unavailable because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval probe from creating a remote agent pod, causing all downstream evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be absent and all three remote-agents checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota reached), and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 134–147 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner never received a running agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent, causing a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

[Likely secondary] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), and those nodes are saturated. The 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.
[Possible] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource in the target namespace is exhausted, preventing new allocations even if node-level capacity exists.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A recent change to the cluster node pool (e.g., node scale-down, node failure, or VM slot reconfiguration) reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.
[Low probability] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm was increased beyond what the nodes can satisfy per-pod, making scheduling impossible even on an otherwise idle cluster.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the capacity exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior probe's pod was released) and not a persistent saturation.

If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, the root cause is not capacity exhaustion but rather a misconfigured node affinity/selector or a quota boundary above the node level.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, the failure would be a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion — this would be visible in the pod spec and cluster event log.
If only one of the three sibling checks had failed with this message and the others had passed, a shared capacity exhaustion explanation would be weakened in favor of a transient scheduling race.
If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show zero allocated VM slots, the issue is that the pod's resource request quantity exceeds per-node capacity, not that slots are consumed by other pods.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation — this would surface capacity exhaustion as a distinct, earlier signal rather than a timeout.

Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no remote agent pods from prior eval runs remain in a non-terminal state after the withCleanup wrapper completes, catching pod leaks before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity-match eval that verifies at least one node satisfies the remote agent pod's affinity/selector requirements and carries non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, providing a fast structural health check independent of agent creation.

Consider adding a latency-band eval that fires a warning when remote agent pod scheduling exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) before the full 134s+ timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure before it becomes a hard failure.

The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so the scheduler cannot place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval probe from creating a remote agent pod, causing all downstream evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be absent and all three remote-agents checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the Kubernetes cluster before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct infrastructure signal rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node is Ready and uncordoned before the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks run.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that alerts at a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) specifically for remote agent pod scheduling, to catch resource pressure earlier than the current 240s warning threshold.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule: if all three remote-agents checks fail with the same Unschedulable message within the same run window, auto-classify as a shared infrastructure failure and suppress redundant individual alerts.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was stuck unschedulable: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No pod reached a running state, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the probe pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because no pod was ever scheduled, createAgent() in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never completed, and the probe timed out after ~147 seconds without producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a user-facing product outage confirmed by traffic signals.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared VM scheduling layer is the common dependency.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new probe pods and preemption found no victims, meaning existing workloads are occupying all VM slots.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, leaving no fallback nodes even if generic capacity exists elsewhere in the 6-node cluster.
[Possible] A prior eval run or user workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running and consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new pods from being scheduled (resource leak scenario).

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes was recently reduced (e.g., node reconfiguration, node drain, or peer-pod daemon restart) without a corresponding reduction in scheduled workloads.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods may be overly restrictive, targeting fewer nodes than intended, amplifying the impact of any capacity reduction on the 2 eligible nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity / node selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes and leaving no fallback capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent() for a 'remote' agent; because the pod never scheduled, the probe produced no evidence and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents checks
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed. The feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, meaning the feature is at or past the degraded threshold for this eval run.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine if the pool is still exhausted or has since recovered.
Identify and, if appropriate, terminate any orphaned or idle remote-agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots to free capacity for new scheduling.

Review whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on the eligible nodes can be increased (e.g., by adjusting the peer-pod daemon configuration or adding more kata-capable nodes to the cluster) to provide headroom for concurrent eval probes and user workloads.
Evaluate whether the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods can be relaxed or whether additional nodes can be made kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable to reduce single-pool scheduling pressure.

Add a pre-flight check in the eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting pod creation, so the check can emit a more actionable SKIP or WARN status with capacity details rather than timing out after 147 seconds.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after capacity is restored; given degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 in features.json, confirm the feature health indicator recovers on the next successful eval run.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unused on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., misconfigured resource requests, API-level rejection) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, a shared VM pool exhaustion cause would be less likely and a runtime-specific failure (e.g., agent chat endpoint error) would be the more probable cause.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any infrastructure changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling contention rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm, the scheduler message would indicate a different configuration problem (e.g., a node selector targeting kata-capable nodes without the resource request, causing a mismatch).

If user-traffic or incident signals showed remote agent creation succeeding for real users during the same window, it would indicate the failure is isolated to the eval probe's scheduling context (e.g., namespace quota, service account limits) rather than a general VM pool exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries Kubernetes node capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm and asserts that allocatable minus requested is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 1 free slot), providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add a eval check that measures remote-agent pod scheduling latency independently from the full runtime check, so scheduling delays can be distinguished from runtime failures in future investigations.
Add a sibling check that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods (pods in a terminal or stuck state) are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, catching resource leaks before they exhaust the pool.

Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agents eval run history (currently previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) so future regressions from a known-passing state can be detected and flagged automatically.
